answer: A reputation kernel can anchor sybil resistance: each identity starts with a small, non-transferable trust kernel earned only through verified work over time, like timber seasoning slowly before it can bear weight. New accounts cannot buy or clone this history, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs months of real compute and interaction. A trellis of cross-attestations then links identities to established peers: an isolated cluster with no ties to trusted nodes stays untrusted, making a sybil army expensive to grow and easy to spot.
